name: AnalyzepRF on volume
summary: Estimates voxel-wise population receptive fields (polar angle, eccentricity, size, R2) from retinotopy fMRI and its stimulus with Kendrick Kay's analyzePRF toolbox.
description: Fits the analyzePRF compressive spatial summation model to each voxel of the fMRI time series given the stimulus aperture. Voxels are restricted to the provided mask or, if none, to the FreeSurfer cortical ribbon in the selected lobes (occipital by default). fMRI can optionally be slice-time and motion corrected and globally regressed. Designed for HCP 7T retinotopy data; the stimulus must match the fMRI timing.

inputs.description: Stimulus aperture as a pixelsX x pixelsY x time NIfTI with values in [0,1].
inputs.requirements: Must match the temporal dimension (TR) of the fMRI.

inputs.description: Optional mask in fMRI space restricting the voxels analysed (for example V1).

outputs.description: pRF maps (polar angle, eccentricity, receptive field size, R2, exponent, gain, mean volume) as NIfTI, plus surface VTKs.

parameters.description: Perform slice-timing and head motion correction on fMRI if not already preprocessed
Repetition time of fMRI (read from the nii header if unspecified)
Conversion factor from pixels to degrees subtended for visual stimulus (16 deg / 200 px for HCP data)
Specifies whether global signal regression (GSR) on input fMRI should be done, conversion to % change from baseline

options.label: per-voxel normalization
options.description: regresses out mean signal per voxel

parameters.description:
Use seedmode -2 and perform very quick PRF analysis

% - When <seedmode> is -2, optimization is not performed and instead the best seed based on the super-grid is returned as the final estimate.

seedmode 0:
% - The first seed is a generic large pRF that is centered with respect to the stimulus, has a pRF size equal to 1/4th of the stimulus extent (thus, +/- 2 pRF sizes matches the stimulus extent), and has an exponent of 0.5.

seedmode 1:
% - The second seed is a generic small pRF that is just like the first seed except has a pRF size that is 10 times smaller.

seedmode 2:
% - The third seed is a "supergrid" seed that is identified by performing a quick grid search prior to optimization (similar in spirit to methods described in Dumoulin and Wandell, 2008).  In this procedure, a list of potential seeds is constructed by 
%   exploring a range of eccentricities, angles, and exponents.  For each potential 
%   seed, the model prediction is computed, and the seed that produces the closest 
%   match to the data is identified.

citations.text: Kay KN, Winawer J, Mezer A, Wandell BA. Compressive spatial summation in human visual cortex. J Neurophysiol 110(2):481-494 (2013).
Zhou J, Benson NC, Kay KN, Winawer J. Compressive temporal summation in human visual cortex. J Neurosci 38(3):691-709 (2018).
Benson NC, et al. The Human Connectome Project 7 Tesla retinotopy dataset: Description and population receptive field analysis. J Vis 18(13):23 (2018).

failure_modes.cause: prf/r2.nii.gz was not produced by the pRF fit.
failure_modes.fix: Check the fMRI, stimulus and mask inputs and the MATLAB log.
